text:
Alice Ramos: Hey team — quick heads up, Spectra (prospect) asked if we can onboard their custom 13B variant for the POC. They care about latency (p95 < 200ms) and want KV-cache across sessions. Can we confirm compatibility and any pricing delta?
Ben Cho: @Alice can you share the model artifact link and quantization plan? most 13B variants we support are q4_* or q8_0.
Alice Ramos: Link: https://files.spectra.corp/models/spectra-13b-v2.tar.gz — they plan to use 8-bit quantization and have a slightly altered tokenizer.
Marco Nguyen: Tokenizer changes are the bigger risk. If token ids differ we'll need tokenizer mapping or to ship a tokenizer adapter. KV cache should be fine as long as the model architecture is standard causal. Any custom attention layers?
Alice Ramos: They say "standard causal, minor layernorm tweak". Not sure about exact RMSNorm vs LayerNorm.
Ben Cho: RMSNorm vs LayerNorm can affect kernel selection and perf. If it's RMSNorm we can still run but might fall back to slower kernels (2-3x). Need a quick model scan. I can run variant-checker tomorrow.
Samir Kaur: Pricing note: custom variants + tokenizer adapter + onboarding engineering is typically billed as a one-time "adapter" fee plus a slightly higher per-token rate for the trial because of nonstandard runtime perf. Estimate: adapter $8k, trial rate +20%. Can confirm after perf scan.
Priya Patel: Security Qs: will they be providing data for hosted inference? If yes we need their SOC2 attestation and a brief data flow diagram. Also KMS requirements?
Alice Ramos: POC will use Dedicated for compliance; they asked if Dedicated can be provisioned in us-west-2. They will provide data via SFTP to our ingest. KMS: customer-managed preferred.
Priya Patel: Dedicated in us-west-2 is fine. For customer-managed KMS we need an infra ticket; it adds ~3 business days to provisioning. Also send over the security questionnaire items we got back.
Ben Cho: Plan of action: 1) I run a compatibility scan (model artifacts + tokenizer) 2) Marco runs a perf pass on a dev GPU profile to check kernel fallback/latency 3) Samir drafts pricing/adapters 4) Priya validates security gating + KMS flow. ETA: 48 hours.
Alice Ramos: Great. @Ben please run `./tools/variant-check --input /tmp/spectra-13b` and paste failures here. If you hit tokenizer mismatch, we can try shipping a tokenizer shim.
Ben Cho: Starting scan now. Quick snippet of results I'll paste when done.
deploy-bot: build-variant-checker #42 started by @ben — https://ci.redwood.dev/builds/42 :robot_face:
Ben Cho: scan summary: tokenization mismatch: 73% tokens matched, 27% OOV mapping required. Architecture: causal, detected layernorm variant: rmsnorm_present=true. Perf hint: fallback kernels likely, expect +120% token latency without quant-tuning. Full logs: https://ci.redwood.dev/artifacts/42/logs/variant-scan.txt
Marco Nguyen: That RMSNorm flag explains it. Next steps: 1) try running an RMSNorm-optimized kernel (alpha) 2) if not available, quant-tune with per-channel scaling to recover perf. I can run a quick perf test: `python perf/run.py --model /artifacts/spectra --batch 1 --seq 512`
Samir Kaur: Given perf risk, adapter fee still $8k but trial per-token uplift to +35% if we need alpha kernels. I'll draft two price bands: standard (+20%) and RMS fallback (+35%).
Priya Patel: Security gating: because they're using customer KMS and Dedicated, we only need the signed AUP + SOC2 snapshot. I'll create the infra ticket for KMS binding (ticket #INF-1723).
Alice Ramos: This is perfect — Ben/Marco, after your tests can you include a short note for the sales demo script (what to call out re: latency differences and fallback behaviors)?
Ben Cho: Yep. I'll add a 3-bullet note and drop it here after perf run.
Marco Nguyen: Perf run complete: p95 token latency (batch=1, seq=512): 320ms with baseline kernels, 160ms using alpha RMSNorm kernel (experimental). Memory looks fine. I attached the numbers in the artifact.
Ben Cho: Demo script bullets: 1) "We validated the variant; it uses RMSNorm — we have an optimized kernel in alpha which meets your 200ms p95 target in our tests." 2) "If alpha kernel isn't permitted we will run fallback kernels with expected +60–100% latency impact." 3) "We can ship a tokenizer shim to ensure stable token ids across sessions."
Alice Ramos: Excellent. Samir — attach the two pricing bands and I'll incorporate into the SOW. Priya — please link INF-1723 to this thread when created.
Priya Patel: INF-1723 created: https://infra.redwood.dev/tickets/INF-1723 — added Emily (infra) and security reviewers.
Samir Kaur: Pricing bands doc: https://sales.redwood.dev/proposals/spectra-poc-pricing-draft — two options listed, adapter $8k + trial rate +20% (alpha included) or adapter $8k + trial rate +35% (no alpha). Comments welcome.
Alice Ramos: Thanks everyone. I'll move to SOW draft and book a customer demo next Tue. Will ping here if anything blocks. :thumbsup:
Ben Cho: Thanks — following up after we triage tokenizer mapping and confirm artifact hash.
Marco Nguyen: FYI I'll open a small PR with the RMSNorm alpha kernel flags if needed.
Priya Patel: Adding checklist: signed AUP, SOC2 attestation, KMS binding complete.
Alice Ramos: Closing for now — will reopen thread if the customer requests private on-prem instead of Dedicated.
